title: Joe Franklin, radio and television, higher prices and Capezio shoes
summary: Joe Franklin and a columnist have Green on air, box-office prices double, theatre investors approach, and Capezio offers free shoes.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: And you had to stand there. You had to stand up like a -- great sentries or something, you know. Like at attention. Like doing reveille and so forth. Of course -- had all kinds of stories going on in the show, see, but they was all mostly based on on-the-town dancing, you see. And he was very pleased and surprised. And even Mr. Joe Franklin, he was -- he heard about it, you know. So, I have to laugh when I think about Joe, you see, because he's -- I knew him since I
was growing, you know. And I was on a radio show in the south.

The first time I saw him was the Orson Well -- he was a youngster. He was a child. The wonder boy. And he could tap dance, this youngster. He really could. But he was with someone. And we became friends, see.

So, that's why (unintelligible) with this idea. I would say, 'Well thank you, sir.' And the next thing I knew, here come the radio people. Some critics, some writer -- he used to do a column called "Broadway after dark." So, he had me like to go over the the Hilton Hotel and broadcast, you know, and interview, you know, over there. He done this twice. So, now the box offices -- I mean they're clamoring for tickets, reservations, you know, building up.
And then something else happened to the show that hadn't happened since Russ Columbo, the matinee idol, you know. The raised the box office price to twice its normal, you know, amount, see.

Then someone else come, you see. This Harry Joe Brown, Junior, and some real estate men from up from Westchester. And they had this house down there where Orson Wells used to broadcast (unintelligible) theater." See, it was the largest seating capacity. And they wanted us to represent the show in their theater, you see. And -- oh, yeah, you know, from the Capezio shoe company, you know. They come back stage and he says, you know -- invited -- gave us an invitation
to all the show members to come to his store and get free shoes, dancing shoes, you know, and the taps, see. I have to-- laughter, you see.

So, eventually later he was going to represent us some way, somewhere. He was going to be a backer of some kind, because someone was with him. But he was on route then at that time. I think he was going to some of these other -- I think Hollywood. Somewhere in California he was going to go about one of his other businesses, you see.

He was out there to catch a -- I think he was on some kind of tour. He had to go somewhere. South America or something. But anyhow, it upheld. So, now we get new shoes, right? And we got this invitation to go on to -- rather, I did because it says "Reminiscing with Chuck Green."

So, the next thing I knew, I was called to come out to the box office. And I had to converse with -- which we call Dada. And he said, how would you like to go on the television, you see. And I went on the television with Joe Franklin, you see. So, it happened that once, and then I got invited to return. So, I had to go back again.
